title: Tenant identity and membership boundary
summary: Create the authoritative tenant, member, role, sector, and lifecycle records that every protected read, command, file, job, and subscription resolves before domain work.
steps: Define immutable tenant and membership IDs with archive and transfer rules.
Resolve tenant context once at the API edge and reject absent or contradictory scope.
Expose a read model that can represent an empty tenant without seeded business data.

positive: A permitted member reads only their tenant projection after a tenant switch.
negative: A supplied tenant ID cannot expose another tenant's record, file, job, or subscription.

doneConditions: Cross-tenant read, write, search, file, and subscription denial tests pass with audit evidence.
requiredEvidence: Tenant-context contract tests, migration record, and a scoped request trace.

title: Authentication, session, and role-capability commands
summary: Implement sign-in, sign-out, session renewal, membership selection, role changes, revocation, and capability evaluation as server-enforced operations.
steps: Model role capabilities separately from client navigation labels.
Require fresh authority for owner and account-recovery actions.
Invalidate command and subscription access immediately after suspension, removal, or session revoke.

positive: A role change changes the next authorized command decision and records actor, reason, and revision.
negative: A stale browser session cannot retain a revoked capability or self-escalate.

doneConditions: Role, revocation, break-glass expiry, and session-renewal integration tests are green.
requiredEvidence: Authorization decision log, session-revocation trace, and controlled role-transition test.

title: Actor, consent, and access-audit envelope
summary: Attach authenticated actor, tenant, request, causation, device/session, and declared test lineage to each protected operation without persisting credentials in business records.
steps: Define an append-only audit envelope and redacted searchable summary.
Require a declared actor and tenant for commands, source reads, exports, and support access.
Model read-state and presence as scoped preferences, never universal authorization or truth.

positive: An authorized privileged read emits an auditable, redacted access event.
negative: A missing actor, unknown test lineage, or stale support grant cannot execute a protected act.

doneConditions: Audit rows retain actor, tenant, command, outcome, and correlation without secret material.
requiredEvidence: Audit query test, redaction test, and expired-support-access test.

title: Canonical record envelopes and identity lifecycle
summary: Establish durable IDs, revisions, archive/redaction rules, retained original identity, and explicit relationships for every system object before any projection is treated as canonical.
steps: Define stable IDs, revisions, source identity, archive, restore, redaction, and foreign-key retention rules.
Create explicit tenant-scoped record tables rather than overloading display names or family keys.
Snapshot immutable commercial facts at the document boundary.

positive: An archived SKU remains reachable from earlier orders with its prior identity intact.
negative: Renaming, archive, or redaction cannot silently reuse an ID or rewrite an issued commercial snapshot.

doneConditions: Identity, archive, restore, and redaction migrations prove referential integrity and tenant scope.
requiredEvidence: Schema migration, lifecycle contract tests, and historical-snapshot replay.

title: Event streams, folds, and replayable projections
summary: Build the event/outbox/projection spine so screens read tenant-authorized materialized facts and historical replay cannot import later knowledge into an earlier business state.
steps: Publish versioned domain events and transactional outbox records after accepted commands.
Build tenant-scoped projectors with cursor, sequence, reset, and rebuild behavior.
Store the effective revision and time used by an order, output, and intelligence projection.

positive: Rebuilding a projection yields the same count, hashes, sequence, and document snapshots.
negative: A late price, alias, or model decision cannot change a replayed historical document.

doneConditions: Event ordering, idempotent outbox, projector lag, and replay parity tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Projection rebuild report, replay fixture result, and outbox reconciliation trace.

title: Command protocol, idempotency, and acknowledged outcomes
summary: Standardize command envelopes, validation, expected revision, idempotency lookup, typed errors, and acknowledgement semantics across every write path.
steps: Define command ID, tenant, actor, expected revision, payload schema, and causal reference fields.
Persist idempotency outcome before responding so unknown outcomes can be resolved safely.
Return typed validation, permission, conflict, pending, failed, and retryable states to every port.

positive: A repeated request ID returns the same accepted outcome without duplicate business effects.
negative: A client cannot choose a total, force a stale overwrite, or display success before an accepted response.

doneConditions: All command handlers share envelope validation and unknown-outcome lookup coverage.
requiredEvidence: Idempotency replay test, revision-conflict test, and client acknowledgement trace.

title: Schema expansion, backfill, and compensating recovery
summary: Make production schema change additive, observable, reversible by compensation where needed, and safe to roll forward during partial failure or a paused migration.
steps: Write expand-only migrations with validation checkpoints and rollback or compensating-event plans.
Run chunked, resumable backfills with tenant/test lineage and durable progress.
Gate contract activation on parity checks rather than migration completion alone.

positive: An interrupted backfill resumes the same cursor and preserves valid prior work.
negative: A migration cannot silently reinterpret historical prices, units, stock, documents, or source bytes.

doneConditions: Isolated forward migration, restore, parity, and compensating recovery exercises are recorded.
requiredEvidence: Migration manifest, checkpointed backfill trace, and recovery drill result.

title: Realtime, offline drafts, and concurrent-edit recovery
summary: Deliver authorized projection notifications, cursor catch-up, constrained offline drafts, and server-resolved concurrent editing without treating presence as a lock.
steps: Publish authorized projection notices with cursors and refetch protected detail through normal reads.
Partition local drafts and confirmed cache by tenant and preserve command/idempotency identity.
Disable high-risk offline commands and provide exact conflict or uncertain-outcome recovery.
Recover an interrupted source review as a tenant-scoped draft with lineage, idempotency identity and current-revision recheck; it cannot replay stock/document/message consequences offline.

positive: A reconnect catches up a permitted projection and preserves a valid unsent low-risk draft.
An interrupted phone-source draft reopens with its unresolved rows and requires current-revision review before a later accepted command.
negative: Offline mode cannot issue documents, send externally, change prices or stock, or force-apply a stale command.
An offline/reopened source draft cannot infer box-to-kg conversion, duplicate a receipt, issue a document or claim seven accepted rows.

doneConditions: Reconnect, cursor-gap, conflict, and tenant-cache isolation tests are green.
JNY-01 interrupted-entry/reopen, source-revision conflict, tenant-isolation and no-duplicate-command cases pass.
requiredEvidence: Offline/reconnect test trace, cursor recovery report, and concurrent-editor test.
Source-review draft recovery trace with tenant isolation, stale revision denial and idempotent retry evidence.

title: Shared sheet, form, menu, and error-state contract
summary: Implement the reusable interaction boundary for Product, Customer, and Albarán sheets: one stable object ID, named layers, pending drafts, permission, loading, empty, error, conflict, archive, and recovery states.
steps: Define object-addressed sheet routes, layered Back/Forward behavior, and return context.
Standardize editable draft lifecycle, authoritative acknowledgement, conflict, and recovery language.
Make each surface render its own state matrix rather than a shared fake object template.
Implement UTL-M01–M08: shared 800×600 viewport-clamped frame, one scroll, fixed actions, icon Back/Close and named substeps.
Preserve edited drafts across nested steps, upload handoff, Close/Back/Escape and assistant coverage of customer chat; reconcile unknown saves by original request ID.

Render select, menu and popover portals through the owning task card child-layer contract above that card; preserve focus/escape semantics and keep one task dialog rather than opening a competing modal.

positive: Opening a related object and returning restores the correct origin, selection, query, scroll, and valid draft.
negative: A sheet cannot silently switch object identity, discard a failed draft, or substitute related-object data.

doneConditions: All three sheet contracts have keyboard, narrow-screen, loading, error, conflict, archive, and deleted/redacted tests.
Every task-frame control has desktop, phone, keyboard, reduced-motion, dirty-close and unavailable-provider evidence.
requiredEvidence: Controlled sheet-state drive, accessible interaction audit, and browser-history trace.

title: Per-control exact-copy and accessible-name framework
summary: Bind canonical label tables to controls, tabs, menus, form fields, provider states, errors, and incomplete states so copy is precise, localized safely, and testable without altering business values.
steps: Register each user-facing control with stable ID, visible label, accessible name, object scope, and state-specific copy.
Separate templated UI copy from tenant names, source text, identifiers, quantities, currencies, and user-entered values.
Require review for missing locale strings and render an honest owed-translation state rather than corrupting data.

positive: A control's accessible name names its object, action, and current state where needed.
negative: A translation pipeline cannot rewrite business data, invent a provider receipt, or silently fall back as a completed locale.

doneConditions: Copy inventory, locale extraction, accessible-name checks, and missing-state copy tests are all linked to control IDs.
requiredEvidence: Copy inventory diff, locale build report, and screen-reader label test.

title: Responsive and assistive interaction baseline
summary: Make the three sheet archetypes and all nested menus, tables, charts, forms, and status announcements usable with keyboard, screen reader, touch, and narrow viewport recovery.
steps: Set shared focus, Escape, Enter, dialog, live-region, touch-target, and reduced-motion rules.
Provide tabular/text alternatives for charts and semantic descriptions for non-decorative artwork.
Test loading, unavailable, error, conflict, permission, and recovery announcements at desktop and narrow viewport.
Make source-review recovery, unknown unit/identity validation and reopened-draft conflict states reachable with named status, focus return and narrow-viewport reading order.
Keep E188 list focus/current geometry inside the one inset destination; on phone keep the focused field, value and next/save action reachable above visualViewport and thumb-dock bounds.

positive: Keyboard-only users can complete an authorized sheet command and hear its confirmed outcome.
A keyboard/touch user can read an unknown SKU/box-kg gap, reopen the scoped draft and reach the permitted review action without losing source context.
negative: Focus cannot disappear behind a sheet, a mobile overlay, a chart, or a pending provider state.
A mobile overlay, error announcement or interrupted review cannot hide the unresolved source fact, lose focus or imply accepted stock.
Full-width hover paint, a clipped quantity/unit terminal, or keyboard-obscured action cannot pass E188 interaction evidence.

doneConditions: WCAG 2.2 AA checks and manual keyboard/screen-reader paths cover every control inventory state.
JNY-01 unknown-unit and interrupted-entry states have accessible names, focus recovery and 390/320 px no-overflow tests.
E188 list, long-line, visualViewport and thumb-dock cases pass at the named desktop and phone viewports.
requiredEvidence: Accessibility report, narrow viewport evidence, and manual assistive-technology checklist.
Assistive-technology and narrow-viewport source-review recovery checklist.
